Checkpoint 01 · Expedition briefing

Signal Checkpoint

The final expedition tests judgement rather than memory. Pause, inspect the strongest evidence and choose an action you can justify.

Today's route

About 60 minutes
1TriageSort messages into safe, check first or report.
2InspectUse four signal lenses on one suspicious email.
3RespondPut the safest response actions in order.
4ImproveRepair a weak but genuine school email.
5QualifyDefend final decisions and secure the badge.

Evidence beats instinct

A polished message can still be dangerous, and a genuine message can contain a typo. Signal Scouts pause, inspect and justify their decision with evidence.

Checkpoint 02 · First-response desk

Safe, Check or Report?

Do not decide from one clue. Read the sender, purpose and context, then choose the proportionate response.

Inbox triage

Required
Safe to useExpected, relevant and from a sensible source.
Check firstPlausible, but something is unexpected or unclear.
ReportClear pressure, deception or attempt to steal information.

Updated school timetable

office@archbishopmg.co.uk

You expected an update. It contains the new times in the message and asks you to speak to your form tutor if unsure.

Account closes in 10 minutes

school-security@outlook-support.example

“Verify your password immediately or every school file will be deleted.” A large sign-in button is included.

Unexpected shared document

pupil.name@archbishopmg.co.uk

A pupil in another class has shared “FunnyVideo” with no explanation. There is no request for a password.

Free gaming laptop

winner@claim-prize.example

You did not enter a competition. It asks for your address and school password to “confirm your identity”.

Library reminder—with a typo

library@archbishopmg.co.uk

It names the book you borrowed and asks you to bring it tomorrow. There is one spelling mistake but no link or request for data.

Unexpected answers file

teacher.name@archbishopmg.co.uk

The sender looks familiar, but you were not expecting “AssessmentAnswers.zip” and the message contains no explanation.

Make all six decisions, then test your evidence.

Four signal lenses

Required
0 characters
Important inferenceGood spelling and professional graphics are not proof of safety. The sender, destination, request and context are stronger evidence.
Checkpoint 04 · Response protocol

What Should Happen First?

The right actions matter, but so does their order. Rearrange the protocol so it protects the account and gives the school useful evidence.

Rebuild the Signal Scout protocol

Required

Use the arrows. Do not open the link or attachment “to check”—that would create the very risk you are trying to investigate.

The protocol is deliberately scrambled.

Why report before deleting?

Reporting gives the teacher or IT team a chance to warn others and block the threat. Follow your school's reporting route, then delete when instructed.

🛑
Never reply to challenge the sender.A reply confirms that your address is active and continues the conversation.
Checkpoint 05 · CTG workshop

Poor Writing Is Not Automatically Phishing

This message is genuinely from a pupil, but it makes the teacher work too hard. Improve its clarity without changing its purpose.

GENUINE MESSAGE
Subjecthelp
sir i cant get my work up can u fix it thx
Notice the distinctionIt is weak communication, but nothing here asks you to click, reveal information or act under pressure.

Close the gap

Required
0 characters
Specific subjectExplains the problem.
Clear structureGreeting, details and sign-off.
Independent actionSays what was already tried.
Checkpoint 06 · Qualification test

Defend the Decision

A Signal Scout can explain a decision. Classify the final three messages and justify one with evidence stronger than “it looks suspicious”.

Final three transmissions

Required

Book reminder

library@archbishopmg.co.uk

Expected reminder, correct borrowed book, no link, and one harmless typo.

Polished Classroom update

classroom-update@google-support.example

Perfect spelling and branding, but asks you to sign in through an unrelated domain.

Unexplained pupil share

pupil.name@archbishopmg.co.uk

The school address is genuine, but the file and reason are unexpected.

Explorer field guide

Key terms

PhishingA deceptive message designed to make someone reveal information, open something harmful or visit a fake service.
DomainThe main website or email address name after the @ symbol, used to help identify the real source.
Link previewThe real destination shown when you hover over a link without clicking it.
UrgencyLanguage that pressures you to act quickly before you can think or verify.
VerifyCheck through a separate trusted route, not through the suspicious message itself.
ReportTell a teacher or the school IT team using the approved school process.
ContextWhether the sender, timing and request make sense in the situation.
EvidenceSpecific details that support a decision rather than a guess or feeling.
